design:
Decisions, each with its reason.

D1. Two places the planner always reads get the rule: the exploring duty, and the `submit_spec_document` entry in the tool section (`_operations()` text, shared by the MCP, shim and HTTP renderings, so one edit covers every access path). Reason: a planner follows what is in its prompt; it does not go looking. Slice 1's own evidence is that the duty sentence was read and ignored, so the wording changes too: from a principle to a per-task step ("for each task you write, list in `files` the repo-relative paths it will edit; where two tasks share a path, chain them with `depends_on`"), placed where the planner decides its tasks.

D2. `aw-tool --help <tool>` prints that tool's complete description; `--list` keeps its shape. Alternative considered: put every full description into `--list`. Rejected: it multiplies the size of the one listing every run may call, and it changes a payload that is read for names and arguments. The recommendation can be overturned at approval. The run's tool-access notice (hub/hub/launchability.py) is told the form exists and that `--list` shows only a first line, because nothing else tells a planner to ask.

D3. No restart while the slice builds. Edits to mcp_server.py and agents.py reach agents only on a Hub's next start (the tool server is pinned per Hub); the build touches code and tests only, and the end-to-end drive runs on a fresh Hub after merge.

Acceptance drive (the operator's, after merge, not run inside this slice): a fresh Hub, a real Haiku planner on the shim path, asked to draft a slice of three features that all edit one file. Pass condition: those tasks are chained with `depends_on`, or the submission's response carries an `unordered_file_overlap` warning naming them. It fails today (F509: two of two runs left them parallel and declared no `files`).

The two tasks are disjoint by file (agents.py; mcp_server.py and launchability.py), so neither needs ordering. Their files are named in each description because the Hub serving this authoring turn predates slice 1 and refuses a `files` field; they carry no `files` list for that reason only. Each names aw-reviewer as reviewer, and each is to run `black --check --target-version py311` and `ruff check` on the files it touched before completing.

Whether the planner would ever run `aw-tool --help <tool>` unprompted is untested; D1 does not rely on it, and FR-4 only tells it the form exists.
Agents read the new text only after a Hub restart (pinned tool server, duty text loaded at start); this was not exercised here.
My worktree predates slice 1 (it lacks the `files` field and F509); I read the merged code and F509 from master with git show, not from a running Hub.

problem: Slice 1's acceptance drive failed (scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md F509). On a fresh Hub with the merged code, a real Haiku planner was asked twice for three features that all edit one file. Both times it left the tasks unordered and declared no `files`; the response carried `"warnings": []`, so the plumbing works and nothing could trigger it. Reading the code shows three places a shim planner can learn about the tool, and slice 1 reached only the one it does not read. (1) `aw-tool --list` prints only the first line of each tool's description (`_call_listing`, hub/hub/mcp_server.py), so the full `submit_spec_document` docstring, which holds the `depends_on` rule and the only documentation of `files`, is unreachable; `aw-tool --help` ignores any further argument and prints one fixed usage text. (2) The tool section of the turn prompt, rendered for the shim by `_shim_lines` from `_operations()` (hub/hub/api/v1/agents.py), lists `tasks` as an argument name and says nothing of `depends_on` or `files`. (3) The exploring duty (`SPEC_PHASE_DUTIES["exploring"]`) does reach the planner and carries slice 1's "Order the tasks" sentence, which the planner did not follow: it states a principle ("may name... chained") not a step the planner performs for each task.

requirements.rationale: Slice 1's drive showed the principle-worded sentence was read and not followed; a step the planner carries out for each task is the wording not yet tried.
requirements.statement: The exploring-phase duty text rendered into a specification turn tells the planner, for each task it writes, to list the repo-relative paths the task will edit in `files`, and to chain with `depends_on` any two tasks that share a path.

requirements.rationale: A shim planner sees the tool only through this section; it listed `tasks` and nothing about the fields that order and declare them.
requirements.statement: The tool section rendered into a run's prompt names `depends_on` and `files` in the entry for `submit_spec_document`, for the shim, MCP and HTTP renderings alike.

requirements.rationale: `--list` keeps only the first line, so the documentation of a tool's arguments is unreachable from the shim; keeping `--list` unchanged protects what already reads it.
requirements.statement: `aw-tool --help <tool>` prints the complete description of that tool; a name that is not a callable tool is refused with a usage error naming it; `aw-tool --help` alone and `aw-tool --list` behave as they did.

requirements.rationale: A planner asks for what it has been told exists; nothing in a run's prompt names the form.
requirements.statement: The tool-access notice given to a run that reaches the Hub through `aw-tool` states that `aw-tool --list` shows only the first line of each tool's description and that `aw-tool --help <tool>` shows the whole.

requirements.rationale: This repository runs the Hub that orchestrates the build; a migration runs at its next restart on live data.
requirements.statement: The change adds no database migration.

summary: Slice 1 shipped `files` and the overlap warning, but a planner that reaches the Hub through `aw-tool` never reads the text that teaches them. This follow-up puts the rule, worded as a per-task step, where that planner reads, and lets it ask `aw-tool` for a tool's whole description.
